work_order.understanding:
This is the first ticket with product code in it, so it does two separable jobs and the second is not optional.

The product job: the users, sessions and login_attempts tables with the first committed migration list; a Drizzle client that is Neon when DATABASE_URL is set and in-process PGlite when it is not; migrations applied on boot behind an advisory lock; GET /api/health whose 200 means a real query answered; email-and-password accounts; sessions in an httpOnly cookie; sign-in rate limiting; a profile; and the five screens (/, /sign-up, /sign-in, /settings, the top bar) with the theme tokens and the ten UI primitives every later screen is built from.

The pipeline job: this is the branch that makes sdlc:verify, sdlc:serve, sdlc:ready and sdlc:seed real. `.sdlc/bin/verify-is-real.mjs` fails a PR carrying product code on ANY sdlc: verb that still matches isTrivialScript. I re-derived the guard myself from `.sdlc/bin/lib/guards.js`: gatingScripts() over the scripts map this order produces returns {sdlc:verify, sdlc:serve, sdlc:seed, sdlc:ready, typecheck, lint} plus the install hooks, and `.github/workflows/ci-verify.yml` runs that guard inside the Unit tests step under pipefail, so a non-zero exit fails the job. With the issue's echo stub for sdlc:seed the trivial set is exactly ['sdlc:seed']; with `node scripts/seed.mjs` it is empty. So the issue's line 'sdlc:seed stays a stub here; piece 9 makes it real' cannot hold on a branch that carries code. scripts/seed.mjs is therefore an HTTP liveness check against /api/health that opens no database handle (a bare `node` cannot import the TypeScript client, and ADR-0002 and ADR-0007 both forbid a second process on the PGlite data directory); piece 9 replaces its body with the POST /api/dev/seed call ADR-0007 specifies. I also checked the reserved-path guard: filling a stub is explicitly allowed once, and every script this order touches is either a stub being filled or a new non-trivial body, so package.json raises no reserved hit.

This version exists because v2 was reviewed and had two blocking defects and one gap that would have hard-failed the run, plus several majors. All are answered here rather than deferred. (1) The qa_script signed out and used a registered email two steps before the only sign-up in the script, so AC-7's only browser verification was unexecutable as written; the sign-up steps now come first, and the byte-identity comparison and the six-then-seventh boundary use two different accounts so their per-key failure rows do not contaminate each other. (2) Under v2's strict-by-default env policy, `npm run dev` and the whole vitest process ran with TABS_ENV unset and hit the throw — TR-22's development-and-CI half was unreachable, and so was the 503 half of AC-2; every entry point that reaches config() now carries the local declaration, in the script and in vitest.config.ts. (3) v2 read the applied set from a migrations table that no file created, so the first boot on an empty database would have thrown before any table existed, and it committed no migration SQL at all — either one kills the boot, and with it AC-1's second half, AC-3, AC-4 and the entire QA script.

The one binding decision recorded for this issue — store the split rule with the expense, and rewrite TR-4 so an edit legitimately replaces an expense's stored payers and shares — concerns piece 3's expense form and piece 4's balances. Nothing here implements it and nothing pre-empts it: there is no expense table, no split type and no amount in this data model. It is honoured by omission and named in out_of_scope.
work_order.root_cause:
Not a defect. The repository is empty by design: package.json holds four verbatim echo stubs, there is no src/, no tsconfig and no test, so no sdlc: verb has anything to run and `.sdlc/bin/verify-is-real.mjs` correctly stands down until product code lands. This ticket is the first landing of product code, which is the exact condition under which that guard starts enforcing — and, verified by running the guard's own gatingScripts()/isTrivialScript() rather than by reading them, the condition under which leaving sdlc:seed a stub turns the branch red.

The defects this order fixes are in the plan, not the repository: v2's QA script was not executable in order, its strict-by-default env policy made TR-22's development half and AC-2's 503 half unreachable in every environment this pipeline actually runs, and its migrator read a bookkeeping table and a SQL list that no file in the plan created.
work_order.approach:
Build in dependency order and wire the verbs last, so that by the time ci-verify's verify-is-real step can fail, every verb is real.

**Data.** `src/db/schema.ts` is the single description: `users` (id uuid, email unique and stored lowercased, password_hash, display_name, default_currency varchar(3), created_at, updated_at), `sessions` (id, user_id, token_hash, expires_at, created_at) and `login_attempts` (id, key_hash, source_hash, succeeded, created_at). The session table stores only the SHA-256 of a 32-byte random token, so that hash is one-way because the input has 2^256 entropy. The email and the source address are low-entropy, so plain SHA-256 there would be reversible by any wordlist and an IPv4 space exhaustible in minutes; both columns are HMAC-SHA-256 keyed by a server-side secret src/lib/env.ts owns, and the claim made about them is exactly that: no email and no address in the clear, and no digest computable without the secret. The first migration is generated by `npm run db:generate` and COMMITTED (drizzle/0000_*.sql plus its meta journal), because ci-verify never runs db:generate and migrate() reads the list from disk at boot — an uncommitted list means an empty database with no tables and a sign-up that 500s. Money columns do not appear in this ticket, so `default_currency` is a currency code, not money.

**One client, two drivers, and one migrator that owns its own bookkeeping.** `src/db/client.ts` exports `createDatabase(driver)` taking an already-constructed PGlite instance or Neon Pool, plus a module-level `db` chosen once at import from the presence of DATABASE_URL and held on globalThis, so dev module reloading cannot open the same data directory twice. No test imports the singleton directly; tests install their own instance on that same globalThis slot through tests/helpers/pglite.ts, which is the seam that lets the real route handler and the real actions run against a throwaway database. `src/db/migrate.ts` exports `migrate(db, migrations)`: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for its own applied-migrations bookkeeping, then `pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('tabs:migrations'))`, then re-read the applied set INSIDE the lock, apply only what is missing in order inside one transaction, release in a finally. Creating the bookkeeping table is migrate.ts's own first statement and it is NOT in schema.ts, because it is migrator state rather than product data and because schema.ts's three tables are the ones the first migration creates. Re-reading inside the lock is the whole point — reading before it is the bug that lets two cold starts both decide a migration is pending. `src/instrumentation.ts` calls it once per server start on the Node runtime, guarded by `process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs'`: Next's own boot hook, not middleware, because middleware runs on the Edge runtime (ADR-0002) and the PGlite WASM must not be bundled (conventions.md).

**Env — what 'production' means here, and why it is not NODE_ENV.** `src/lib/env.ts` exports `loadEnv(source)`, taking the environment as an ARGUMENT so both halves are testable without mutating process.env, and a lazily-memoised `config()`. It never throws on import. `TABS_ENV=local` means 'this boot is local, CI or QA': substitute the documented local defaults — DATABASE_URL unset, which selects in-process PGlite, and TABS_HMAC_KEY set to a fixed development-only constant whose name and log line both mark it as not a secret — and log one line naming each default used. ANY other value, including unset, is strict: every variable in the required set (DATABASE_URL, TABS_HMAC_KEY) must be present, and if any is missing, startup stops with one message naming every missing one and stating that `TABS_ENV=local` is the way out. The polarity is deliberate and opposite to the intuitive one — strict by default, because a real deployment that forgets a variable must fail loudly rather than silently come up on in-memory PGlite and lose every write on the next cold start.

The consequence that decides the whole boot story: EVERY entry point that reaches config() must declare itself local, because the harness sets nothing. `sdlc:serve` carries `TABS_ENV=local` on both halves; `dev` carries it too, because instrumentation's register() DOES run under `next dev` (Next skips it only under NEXT_PHASE=phase-production-build, which is `next build`), so a bare `next dev` on a clean checkout would otherwise throw and contradict TR-22's development half. The vitest process declares it in vitest.config.ts rather than in package.json alone, because `sdlc:verify` invokes `vitest run` directly and would bypass a prefix on the `test` script. `build` deliberately does not carry it: validation is a boot-time call that `next build` never reaches, and the prefix there would be belt-and-braces. scripts/seed.mjs mirrors the polarity rather than inverting it — it refuses unless TABS_ENV is unset or 'local', so a real deployment whose TABS_ENV is 'production', or misspelled as 'prod', fails closed. (The two answers are different questions and both are safe at unset: 'may this server come up on defaults?' — yes only if declared local; 'may this process touch the app?' — yes only if the app is running on local defaults.)

**Auth, and the one seam four criteria hang on.** `src/lib/cookies.ts` is the named seam: one `cookieStore()` accessor that reads next/headers' `cookies()` when a request scope exists and an async-local store when a test has installed one, with `createSessionCookie` and `clearSessionCookie` as the only two writers. `src/lib/auth.ts` never imports next/headers directly — without this file, `cookies()` throws outside a request scope, the test shim is dead code, and AC-5, AC-6, AC-7 and AC-11 fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the product. auth.ts itself holds the whole of auth: scrypt at N=2^17, r=8, p=1 with a 16-byte random salt and the parameters carried in the stored string (ADR-0006); session create/resolve/revoke; the rate-limit predicates; and `requireUser()`, which reads the cookie through cookieStore() and redirects to /sign-in when there is no live session. Sign-up, sign-in and sign-out are Server Actions in `src/app/actions/auth.ts`; the profile save is `src/app/actions/profile.ts`. All four return `{ok:false, fieldErrors, formError}` on an expected failure rather than throwing. The session cookie is httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, path /, maxAge 30 days, unconditionally — Chrome and Firefox both treat http://localhost as a secure context and store a Secure cookie there, so TR-10 holds in QA as written; if a browser ever does not, that is a finding to report, not a deviation to introduce.

**Rate limiting — both boundaries, stated once each, in terms of an attempt.** IAC-7's two sentences are only simultaneously true if the account limit refuses wrong passwords without ever locking a correct one out. **Account: the account limit refuses a wrong password once six failures for that key already exist in the window, so the seventh wrong attempt inside the window is refused, and a correct password is accepted regardless of the count.** **Source: the source limit refuses once twenty failures from that source already exist in the window, so the twenty-first attempt inside the window is refused without verifying the password at all.** Both sentences are repeated verbatim in AC-7, in src/lib/auth.ts and in both rate-limit test files; the QA script names the seventh and the twenty-first. Attempts one through six are verified and each records a failure; the seventh is verified, is wrong, records no seventh row and returns the same message.

Both predicates count rows with `succeeded = false`, because TR-11's subject is failed sign-ins. Every attempt still writes a row carrying its true `succeeded` value — the account predicate filters on `succeeded = false`, and a successful sign-in deletes that account's failure rows so the account bucket is not left polluted. Counting successful sign-ins against the source bucket would refuse a correct password for having signed in twenty times in fifteen minutes, which is a lockout the requirement does not ask for. The window is WINDOW = 15 minutes sliding over `created_at`, and a row is inside it when `created_at > now - WINDOW`: strictly greater, so a row exactly fifteen minutes old is outside and is pruned, which is what keeps the boundary testable. ACCOUNT_LIMIT = 6, SOURCE_LIMIT = 20.

The account limit saves no CPU, and the plan says so rather than leaving an implementer to guess: verifying is what costs anything, and a correct password must still be verified to be accepted. The work-saving limit is the source-keyed one, which is different in kind — flooding is a denial of service, not a credential guess — so it hard-refuses and skips the scrypt comparison entirely. **When no address can be determined the source limit does not apply and the account limit carries the request alone.** That is deliberate: `next start` on loopback sets neither x-forwarded-for nor x-real-ip, so a shared bucket would let one flood refuse every legitimate user of a deployment, and would make QA's own repeated sign-ins trip a global lock. All four refusals — unknown email, wrong password, account-limited, source-limited — return the identical message.

**Retention.** Every attempt writes a login_attempts row by design, so `checkRateLimit` deletes rows older than WINDOW at the top of the call and `resolveSession` deletes the row it resolves once it is past expires_at. Both are index-supported and both keep each predicate's query bounded.

**Screens.** A route group `src/app/(app)/` holds the signed-in shell: its layout calls requireUser() and renders the shell, and it contains `/` and `/settings`. Sign-in and sign-up sit outside it and are deliberately reachable by a signed-in visitor as well — no redirect is added in this ticket, because the QA script's double-submit step needs the sign-up form, and a redirect there would make that step unrunnable. `/` is the empty state exactly as docs/ui.md words it — "You're not in any groups yet." with Create group as the single action and a quieter second line about opening an invite link — because there are no groups yet and no group query runs. The ten primitives are the design system's floor and the ticket names them, so they are built here; two of them (money, dialog) have no caller in this ticket and that is stated per file rather than hidden. The home empty state and the shell are extracted as synchronous presentational components (`src/components/home-empty.tsx`, `src/components/shell.tsx`) that the pages render and the component test composes, because a Server Component that awaits cookies() cannot be rendered by @testing-library/react and importing a page would construct a real PGlite at import time. The busy state is Client Component work and is named: `src/components/auth-form.tsx` and `src/components/settings-form.tsx` carry 'use client' and the pending state via useActionState, `src/app/(app)/error.tsx` carries 'use client' as Next requires, and `src/components/ui/dialog.tsx` carries it for its focus trap. Button itself stays a presentational component taking a busy label and a disabled prop, so conventions.md's 'use client only where there is genuine interaction' is applied deliberately.

**Verbs, last.** package.json gets typecheck, lint, test, build, dev, db:generate and the four real sdlc: bodies, every version pinned exactly per conventions, plus a committed package-lock.json for ci-verify's `npm ci`. `verify.typecheck` and `verify.lint` are empty in `.sdlc/config.yml` and that file is reserved, so typecheck and lint run through sdlc:verify in the order conventions.md fixes rather than as separate ci-verify steps; the checks still run, on every PR.

files.change: The whole of auth, so its security properties are readable in one file. `hashPassword`/`verifyPassword` on `crypto.scryptSync` at N=2^17, r=8, p=1 with a 16-byte random salt, stored as one string carrying the parameters, the salt and the hash (ADR-0006). `createSession` generates 32 random bytes, stores only their SHA-256 and returns the raw token for the cookie. `resolveSession(token)` returns the user only if the row exists and has not expired, deleting an expired row it touches. `revokeSession(tokenHash)` deletes the row. `keyFor(email)` and `sourceFor(address)` are HMAC-SHA-256 over the trimmed-lowercased email and the address, keyed by the env module's secret — NOT plain SHA-256, because both inputs are low-entropy and reversible by wordlist or exhaustive search. Cookie reads and writes go through src/lib/cookies.ts and never through next/headers directly. `checkRateLimit(email, address)` deletes rows older than WINDOW at the top, then returns 'ok' | 'account' | 'source' against ACCOUNT_LIMIT = 6, SOURCE_LIMIT = 20, WINDOW = 15 minutes, all sliding over `created_at`, with a row inside the window when `created_at > now - WINDOW` (strictly greater, so a row exactly fifteen minutes old is outside). Both predicates count only rows with `succeeded = false`: 'account' once six failures for that key already exist in the window, so the seventh wrong attempt is refused; 'source' only when an address was actually determined and twenty failures from it already exist, so the twenty-first attempt is refused without verifying the password. Counting successes would lock out a user who signed in twenty times in fifteen minutes, which is not what TR-11 asks for — TR-11's subject is failed sign-ins. `requireUser()` reads the cookie through cookieStore(), resolves the session and redirects to /sign-in when there is none. The cookie is set httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, path /, maxAge 30 days, unconditionally, and the cookie NAME is a single constant defined here so the two writers and the tests cannot disagree about it.
files.why: ADR-0005 and project.md name this one file. The HMAC, the constants and both attempt-level boundaries are stated here rather than left to the implementer, because all three are decisions and none is recoverable from the code afterwards.

files.change: Three Server Actions: signUp, signIn, signOut. Each parses its input with a Zod schema in this same file and returns `{ok:false, fieldErrors, formError}` on an expected failure rather than throwing. signUp trims and lowercases the email, bounds it (a maximum length and a shape check — keyFor HMACs the whole value and the column is unbounded text), enforces a password length bound (8–200 characters — scryptSync runs over the whole input, so an unbounded body spends the quarter second per attempt the source limiter exists to ration) and a display-name length bound, and inserts with `onConflictDoNothing` on users.email so the unique constraint is authoritative and a duplicate maps to `fieldErrors.email` with the same wording the pre-check uses; the pre-check is a nicety for the message, never the guarantee. It creates the user and its session in one transaction. signIn follows exactly this order and no other: prune rows older than WINDOW; if an address was determined and the source bucket is already at twenty failures, hard-refuse with the generic message having skipped scrypt entirely; otherwise verify the password — ALWAYS, because a correct password is accepted however many failures precede it — then on success write a row with succeeded = true, delete that account's succeeded = false rows and create the session, and on failure record a new row unless the account bucket is already at ACCOUNT_LIMIT, in which case no seventh row is written. Every one of those exits returns the identical message. signOut revokes the row and clears the cookie. None of the three redirects an already-signed-in visitor away: the pages render for one, because the QA script's double-submit step needs the sign-up form.
files.why: conventions.md: writes are Server Actions, one file per noun, validated with Zod, returning a typed result the form renders. The insert being authoritative rather than the pre-check is a read-then-insert race that otherwise surfaces as a 500 on exactly the double-submit QA is asked to perform. The explicit order is where the off-by-one becomes a decision rather than an accident.

files.change: GET with `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`. It resolves its config and its client through the same accessors the rest of the app uses, so a test can install its own PGlite and its own resolved config. It then runs a real query (`select 1`), timing it, and returns 200 `{status:'ok', database:'ok', latencyMs}` with a positive measured latencyMs. EVERY failure is a 503, never a throw: a query failure returns `{status:'degraded', database:'error', error: <the fixed sentence 'the database could not be reached'>}`, and a config failure returns `{status:'degraded', database:'unconfigured', error: <a different fixed sentence naming that the application is not configured>}` — a different sentence, because claiming a database fault when the process was never configured is a lie QA would chase. Neither sentence is ever the driver's own text, and the redaction strips anything resembling a connection string, a password, or a host with credentials before serialisation. A config failure still fails `sdlc:ready`, because curl -f treats 503 as failure — which is the whole tripwire this route carries. No session required.
files.why: IAC-2, and it is what sdlc:ready polls: a 200 here has to mean the database answered, or every later ticket's readiness check is theatre. Catching the config failure rather than letting it propagate is what keeps AC-2's 503 half testable in a process where TABS_ENV is not set, and what keeps a misconfigured boot from answering 200.

files.change: A plain Node ESM script, no build step. It REFUSES unless `TABS_ENV` is unset or exactly 'local' — printing that seeding is available only where the application itself boots on local defaults, and exiting non-zero otherwise. Mirroring env.ts's polarity rather than inverting it is deliberate: a NODE_ENV-keyed guard would refuse under `next start`, which sets NODE_ENV=production and is the only way this script is ever run; a `TABS_ENV === 'production'` guard would fail OPEN on a deployment whose TABS_ENV is misspelled, which is the exact failure TR-26 forbids. Unset means local, and a real deployment that forgot TABS_ENV would already be refusing to boot. Otherwise it performs an HTTP GET of http://localhost:3000/api/health, prints the status it received, and exits 0 on 200 or non-zero otherwise. It opens no database handle, imports nothing from src/, and writes no rows; a comment states that piece 9 replaces this body with the POST /api/dev/seed call ADR-0007 specifies.
files.why: sdlc:seed has to be non-trivial or verify-is-real fails the branch, and `node scripts/seed.mjs` alone already satisfies isTrivialScript — I read guards.js and the liveness body is not what passes the guard, the command string is. The body is here because it is safe, it honours ADR-0007's dependency on the app being up, and it cannot corrupt a PGlite data directory the way a direct-connect seed would.

Every entry point that reaches config() declares itself local: sdlc:serve on both halves, `npm run dev`, `npm test` and a bare `npx vitest run` — so a developer with nothing set and a runner with nothing set both come up, and only a process that has not declared itself local is strict.

Then, with nothing exported: `npx vitest run` exits 0 and `npm run dev` starts and serves /sign-in. The second sentence is the regression guard for the environment policy and is what makes every browser criterion below reachable.

acceptance.check: Integration tests run against a fresh in-process PGlite with no network: the migrations apply to an empty database including the first-boot case, re-applying is a no-op, the health endpoint answers both 200 and 503, and the session and rate-limit rules above hold.
acceptance.how_to_verify: `npm test` on a runner with no DATABASE_URL and no Postgres installed; the suite passing at all is the proof, since every case would fail on a network dependency. The single sanctioned way a test reaches the database is tests/helpers/pglite.ts, which installs its instance before any module import — a test that reaches the client singleton any other way has built a defect, not a shortcut.

qa_script: The app is already built and running on http://localhost:3000 by the pipeline, started through `npm run sdlc:serve`, which sets TABS_ENV=local so a production build boots with no DATABASE_URL and no configured secrets. If that boot had failed, this script could not start. Confirm `npm run sdlc:ready` exits 0 before touching a browser. If it does not, stop and report blocked, and paste the app's startup log line — if migrations or configuration failed, that line is the whole diagnosis and wait-ready will otherwise report it as an environment failure.

curl -i http://localhost:3000/api/health. Expect 200 and a body of {status, database, latencyMs} with latencyMs > 0. Then confirm no part of the body contains 'postgres://', a password or a host with credentials. Confirm the app's startup log line names the local defaults it used.
Open http://localhost:3000/ with no cookie. Expect a redirect to /sign-in — not a rendered page and not a 500.
Open /sign-in. Tab through the whole form. At every stop confirm a visible 2px focus ring, and confirm the page has exactly one h1. Confirm the email input is focused on arrival.

Sign up at /sign-up as qa1@example.invalid with a password of your choosing. Expect to land signed in on / with the empty state "You're not in any groups yet.", a single Create group action and exactly one h1. This account is the one the rate-limit step uses; the next step creates a second account for the byte comparison, because the account limit is per key and the two sequences would otherwise contaminate each other's failure rows.
Use the Create group action. It is a link into a screen this ticket does not build (groups are piece 2) — confirm it is present and labelled, and do NOT report its destination as a bug.
Sign out through the top bar. Sign up a SECOND account, qa2@example.invalid, and sign out again — you now hold two registered accounts, which the last two steps need.

With qa2 registered and signed out: sign in with an email that does not exist, nobody@example.invalid. Note the exact status code and the exact message text. Then sign in as qa2@example.invalid with a deliberately wrong password. Compare BOTH the status codes and the messages character for character — they must be identical, with no hint that the account exists.

Sign in SEVEN times in a row as qa1@example.invalid with a wrong password. The first six are refused with the generic message and each records a failure; the seventh is refused with the identical message and records nothing further — that identical seventh refusal is the boundary AC-7 fixes. Then sign in once with the CORRECT password and expect it to be ACCEPTED. Report it if a legitimate sign-in is locked out — that is the assertion tests/integration/rate-limit.test.ts exists to protect.

Go to /settings. Change the display name to 'QA Tester' and the default currency, save, and confirm the new name appears in the top bar and on /settings. Then force a failure (submit with the name emptied, and separately with the currency set to 'EURO') and confirm the error sits next to the field, that 'EURO' is refused rather than truncated to 'EUR', that what you typed elsewhere is kept, and that no raw error or stack trace is shown.
Sign out through the top bar. Confirm the cookie is cleared, then re-paste the old cookie value into the browser and open / — expect the sign-in redirect, not the home screen.

Submit the sign-up form twice in quick succession with a fresh address, qa3@example.invalid (two tabs, or a slow-cpu throttle with a repeated primary-button press). Expect the button to disable and read 'Creating account…', exactly one account to exist, a clear field-level message rather than a 500, and no unhandled error.

On each of the four screens, zoom to 200% and confirm no horizontal scrolling and no lost content; then resize to 360px wide and confirm the sign-in and sign-up cards span the width with no card border and the home empty state stays readable.

Do NOT report as bugs in this ticket: the source-address rate limit being inert (there is no proxy in front of the app here, so no request has a determinable source address, and that is a documented decision rather than an omission); the app booting on local defaults rather than refusing (sdlc:serve declares the boot local, which is the documented answer to what 'production' means here); the qa_auth.signup_url of /signup returning 404 (the route is /sign-up; .sdlc/config.yml is a reserved path this ticket may not edit); sign-out living outside a profile menu (no menu primitive exists yet); the money, dialog and skeleton primitives having no or partial callers; and anything about groups, invites or amounts.

alternatives_considered.approach: Gate the required-variable check on NODE_ENV=production, as v1 did.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It makes the app refuse to boot in the only environment it is ever run in. `next start` sets NODE_ENV=production itself, and .sdlc/config.yml's env.boot is `npm run sdlc:serve`. Nothing in .sdlc/bin, .sdlc/qa or .github sets NODE_ENV or DATABASE_URL. So the app threw during startup, /api/health never answered, sdlc:ready failed, and every browser criterion plus the whole qa_script died at step one. An env check keyed on a variable the platform sets for you is not a production check.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep NODE_ENV governing and make sdlc:serve supply a DATABASE_URL and a real HMAC key for local QA.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would mean QA booting against a Postgres the harness does not provide, and it forfeits the ticket's central claim: TR-21 and ADR-0002 exist so that development, CI and QA need nothing installed and no account. It also makes IAC-3's PGlite half unreachable in the one environment QA can run.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make the required-variable check opt-in — validate only when REQUIRE_SECRETS=1 is set, so nothing throws unless a deploy asks for it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fails open. A deployment that sets DATABASE_URL but forgets the arming variable comes up silently on in-memory PGlite, writes everything to a database that dies with the next cold start, and logs nothing — the exact failure TR-22 exists to prevent, arriving through the door the fix opened. Inverting the polarity costs one `!==` and puts the failure where a deployer will see it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Use VERCEL_ENV, or NODE_ENV plus a loopback check, to tell a real deployment from QA.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: env.ts runs before any request exists, so a request-boundary signal has nothing to bind to. VERCEL_ENV would make the check correct on Vercel and meaningless everywhere else, including the self-hosted production deployment that most needs it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Let the health route propagate a config() failure as a throw (v2's design), on the argument that failing loudly is the tripwire.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It makes AC-2's 503 half unreachable in every environment this pipeline runs, because the vitest process — like every other process here — has TABS_ENV unset and is therefore strict. The tripwire survives the alternative anyway, because curl -f treats 503 as failure, so catching the failure costs the boot nothing and buys a testable AC-2 and a health endpoint that answers rather than 500s.

alternatives_considered.approach: Count successful sign-ins against the source-keyed limit, as the critique's remedy proposed.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: TR-11's subject is failed sign-ins: 'Failed sign-ins are rate-limited per account and per source address.' Counting successes would refuse a correct password for having signed in twenty times in fifteen minutes — a lockout of exactly the kind the account-limit design exists to avoid, and one no criterion asks for. The `succeeded` column still earns its place: every attempt writes a row with its true value, both predicates filter on `succeeded = false`, and a successful sign-in clears that account's failure rows. The critique's diagnosis was right and its prescription was not.

alternatives_considered.approach: Let the health route return the same fixed sentence for a missing variable and an unreachable database.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would report a configuration fault as a database fault, and QA's job is to drive a live app — a sentence that sends the reader to the wrong subsystem is worse than no sentence. Two fixed sentences, neither of them the driver's text, keeps AC-2 whole and keeps both trips failing.

alternatives_considered.approach: Let the actions and the health route import next/headers directly and have the test shim patch the module.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `cookies()` throws outside a request scope and the natural implementation is the one that works in (app)/layout.tsx, so the shim would be dead code and four acceptance criteria would depend on a module patch the plan never described. A named src/lib/cookies.ts with one accessor and two writers is the seam; the alternative is a test that passes or fails on mocking rather than on product behaviour.

alternatives_considered.approach: scripts/seed.mjs connects to the database and reports which driver is in use, as the first proposal specified.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `sdlc:seed` is `node scripts/seed.mjs` and nothing in this order compiles TypeScript for it, so the script cannot import src/db/client.ts at all; and even if it could, ADR-0007 states a seed must reach the database through the app's HTTP endpoint and ADR-0002 states that a second process on the same PGlite directory corrupts it. A database handle is not what makes a seed real.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave sdlc:seed as the echo stub the issue's Out of scope section asks for and let CI decide.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: I re-ran `.sdlc/bin/lib/guards.js`'s own gatingScripts() and isTrivialScript() against the exact scripts map this order produces: the trivial set is ['sdlc:seed'] with the stub and empty without it, and ci-verify runs that guard inside the Unit tests step under pipefail. The branch whose subject is that CI works would be the branch that turns it red. One correction to the council's own reasoning, which the critique caught and I confirmed by reading guards.js: isTrivialScript splits on &&/||/; and demands every segment be exit/true/:/echo, so the COMMAND `node scripts/seed.mjs` already passes the guard and the liveness body is not load-bearing. The body stays because it is safe and ADR-0007-aligned, not because CI needs it — the plan claimed the latter and was wrong about the mechanism while right about the outcome.

alternatives_considered.approach: Hard-lock an account for the window after N failures, returning 429 once it trips.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It contradicts the second sentence of IAC-7 — a correct password on the next attempt is accepted — and it hands an attacker a denial of service against a named user for the price of six guesses. Only the source-keyed limit hard-refuses, because there the threat is flooding rather than guessing.

alternatives_considered.approach: Put unknown source addresses into one shared bucket so the source limit applies everywhere.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `next start` on loopback sets neither x-forwarded-for nor x-real-ip, so in QA and in local development every request has the same absent address; a shared bucket would let one flood refuse every legitimate user of a deployment, and would make QA's own repeated sign-ins trip a global lock. Exempting unknown sources means the source limit is inert until a proxy sets the header, which is stated in the code, in risks and in the QA script's do-not-report list rather than left to be discovered.

alternatives_considered.approach: Refuse the sixth wrong attempt rather than the seventh, the off-by-one variant the v1 reviewer offered as equally available.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Both readings satisfy IAC-7 in prose, which is exactly why v1's two tests were free to disagree. This order takes the variant where six failures EXIST before the limit bites, because it makes ACCOUNT_LIMIT = 6 mean what its name says and makes the row count and the attempt count agree at the boundary. The same reasoning is applied to the sibling constant, which the critique noted v2 had left in the old ambiguous phrasing.

alternatives_considered.approach: Use Drizzle's built-in migrator instead of a hand-written one.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It reads the applied set and then applies, with no advisory lock around the pair, so two cold starts can both read 'pending' and both apply. IAC-3 asks for the lock specifically, and the bookkeeping table is hand-written alongside it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Use citext for the email column so uniqueness is case-insensitive at the database rather than by lowercasing in the action.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It makes the uniqueness guarantee depend on an extension PGlite does not necessarily carry, so the local guarantee and the production one would differ — precisely the divergence ADR-0002 warns about.

alternatives_considered.approach: Render the four screens directly in a component test, as the first proposal specified.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The signed-in shell awaits requireUser(), @testing-library/react cannot render an async Server Component, and importing any page transitively constructs a real PGlite at import time. The presentational markup is extracted instead, and the test composes the two extracted components into a real screen — which is also the only composition that can prove 'exactly one h1' rather than 'at most one per component'.

alternatives_considered.approach: An auth library (Auth.js/NextAuth) for sessions and rate limiting.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Already decided and recorded in project.md and ADR-0005. Re-deciding it here would re-litigate an ADR, which is what .sdlc/memory/decisions/README.md exists to prevent.

assumptions: That verify-is-real.mjs's current behaviour is the intended one and the issue's 'sdlc:seed stays a stub' is the stale half. I verified the code path by running the guard's own gatingScripts/isTrivialScript against the exact scripts this order proposes, so the CI consequence is established; what I cannot establish is which of the two the human intended. If the stub is genuinely wanted, the fix is a one-line change in .sdlc/config.yml or verify-is-real.mjs, both reserved paths — which is itself the reason the script is the wrong half of the disagreement.

That `pg_advisory_lock` and `hashtext` are available on PGlite 0.5.8. PGlite is Postgres compiled to WASM and ADR-0004 assumes the lock works, but there is no database in this environment to run it against. If either is missing, the fallback is a `select ... for update` on the bookkeeping row held in the transaction, which changes one function in src/db/migrate.ts and nothing else in this order moves.

That `drizzle-kit generate` produces SQL that runs unchanged on PGlite as well as on Neon 16. If it emits anything PGlite rejects, the committed SQL in drizzle/ is hand-edited and the schema stays the source of truth — which tests/integration/migrations.test.ts will catch on the first CI run rather than in production.

That Next 16.3's instrumentation register() is invoked at server start under `next start` and `next dev` and NOT during `next build`. Both the proposal and the critique checked the published tarball and agree: the hook is detected by the build, and registerInstrumentation returns early only under NEXT_PHASE=phase-production-build, which is the build. This is load-bearing in two directions — it is why env validation is a boot-time call behind loadEnv(source) that never throws at import, and it is why `dev` needs the TABS_ENV=local prefix while `build` does not. The design is also safe if the reading is wrong, because a module that never throws on import cannot break a build.

That a throw inside register() actually stops the server rather than being logged and swallowed. If Next catches a rejecting register() and continues booting, the second gate is already in place: GET /api/health resolves config() and answers 503, so sdlc:ready's curl -f fails and QA reports blocked rather than driving an app that should not be running. Both paths were specified so the strict check cannot be defeated by an unverified assumption about the framework.

That the QA runner's browser treats http://localhost as a secure context and will therefore store a Secure cookie, which TR-10 requires unconditionally. Chrome and Firefox both do. If the runner's browser does not, this order does not open an exception: that is a finding to report, not a deviation to introduce, and omitting Secure in development is explicitly not authorised.

That the rate-limit constants and the window operator are the plan's to set: ACCOUNT_LIMIT = 6 (from IAC-7), SOURCE_LIMIT = 20, WINDOW = 15 minutes sliding, and a row is inside the window when `created_at > now - WINDOW`. They are named rather than left to the implementer because 'inside the window' with no duration and no operator cannot be tested at the boundary.

That 'six failed sign-ins are refused and a correct password on the next attempt is accepted' means the account limit refuses wrong passwords without locking the account out — the only reading under which both sentences hold. The source limit's hard refusal, its exemption for undetermined addresses, and its counting of failed attempts only are this order's decisions and are stated in approach, in src/lib/auth.ts and in the QA script.

That the health route resolving its config and its client through accessors is a sufficient seam for the tests, and that a route handler's GET is directly callable in vitest once cookies() is out of the picture. AC-2 is the criterion that depends on this; if Next's route wrapper turns out to make GET uncallable outside a request, the fallback is asserting 200 and 503 through a real HTTP call to the booted app in QA, and AC-2's verify moves to browser — a change of harness, not of requirement.

That installing with --ignore-scripts leaves every dependency usable — the assumption the whole stack rests on and the reason Prisma and Argon2 were rejected in the project brief. Drizzle, PGlite, Neon, Zod and Tailwind are pure JavaScript; the first CI run on this branch is what proves it rather than my reading of their manifests.

That a human running bare `next start` locally, without TABS_ENV=local, should get the strict throw. This order chooses it over the friendlier alternative because the message names TABS_ENV=local as the way out, so the failure teaches the command, and the alternative is a check that only fires when someone remembers to arm it. `npm run dev` is prefixed, so the ordinary local command is not affected.
unknowns: Whether `TABS_ENV=local cmd` prefixes work under whatever shell the pipeline uses to invoke env.boot. It is POSIX-sh syntax and correct for npm script execution on Linux, which is where compose-mode QA runs; it would not work on a Windows cmd shell, and a self-hosted Windows developer would need the cross-env form.

Whether a Vercel deployment can hold the Neon Pool singleton across a cold start well enough for the advisory lock to be meaningful there. Nothing in this repository can answer it — there is no Vercel project and no Neon database yet. What this ticket guarantees is that the same migration list and the same lock run in every environment, which is the part that is testable.

Whether PGlite's single-connection model makes IAC-3's two-concurrent-cold-starts case genuinely provable. The integration test asserts the advisory lock is observable while held, which is the thing the code is responsible for; it cannot prove true multi-connection contention, because one PGlite serialises two calls regardless. The contention itself is only provable on Neon.

Which currencies must be supported at launch. project.md records this as an open question and assumes any ISO 4217 code; the settings field accepts exactly three letters rather than a closed list, so the eventual picker is a product decision this ticket does not pre-empt.

Whether the top bar's profile affordance should be a menu or a direct link. docs/ui.md's Navigation example mentions a profile link and its Destructive-action section implies a menu; with no menu primitive in the design system, this order renders a profile link plus a sign-out control and revisits it when a menu is genuinely needed.

Whether ci-verify's absent build step leaves any hole in what the branch proves. `.sdlc/config.yml` sets verify.build to the empty string and ci-verify.yml skips the Build step when it is, so `next build` runs only inside sdlc:serve, which QA's env.boot invokes and ci-verify does not. AC-1 is therefore proved in two halves and names both.
risks: This order knowingly contradicts a line in the issue's Out of scope section: scripts/seed.mjs exists where the issue says it stays a stub. It is deliberate, the guard consequence was verified by running the guard's own code, and it is in understanding so nobody has to rediscover it. The exposure is pipeline-wide rather than branch-wide, since hasProductCode() counts any tracked file outside .sdlc/, .github/, docs/, bin/sdlc and package*.json — which is an argument for the maintainer fixing the reserved file rather than for this ticket bending around it. Until that happens, this branch's CI is red if the stub is kept.

A later ticket that finds scripts/seed.mjs unneeded and deletes it will trip the reserved-path guard rather than a test failure, because reservedChanges treats removing a real gating script as a change needing a person. Piece 9 replaces the body; it does not delete the file.

Strict-by-default env validation is a standing regression surface for every ticket after this one: any boot that forgets TABS_ENV=local now stops at startup with a throw, by design. The scripts that need the prefix carry it, but a future compose-mode boot or a new entry point added by a later ticket must be checked, and the error message is the only thing telling a person which variable they forgot.

ADR-0007 words the seed endpoint's guard as 'refuses to run when NODE_ENV is production'. Under a `next start` boot NODE_ENV is always production, so when piece 9 writes POST /api/dev/seed that guard would refuse to seed the QA environment the seed exists to serve — the identical defect this order just fixed one layer down. ADR-0007 is a reserved path this ticket may not edit, so the fix belongs to piece 9 and to whoever maintains the ADRs; the discriminator has to be TABS_ENV.

The build that CI proves is typecheck and lint, not `next build`. verify.build is empty in a reserved config, so the production build is proved by QA against the same commit rather than by ci-verify. AC-1 is written as two halves for that reason.

Two of the ten primitives — money and dialog — have no caller in this ticket; skeleton has exactly one, in (app)/loading.tsx. Building them is what the ticket asks for and what keeps the design system's floor in one place; the cost is code nothing exercises yet, stated per file rather than left to be discovered.

SCrypt at N=2^17 takes roughly 128 MB and a quarter second per verification (ADR-0006). That makes sign-in the most expensive thing the app does, and it is why the source limit skips verification entirely, why the password input is length-bounded, and why the account limit is stated as NOT saving CPU. It also means the auth and rate-limit suites take tens of seconds — the rate-limit case alone performs seven verifications — and a reviewer should not read that as a hang. vitest.config.ts caps the parallelism so the memory does not compound.

Migrations applied on boot mean the first request after a deploy pays the cost and a failed migration is a boot error rather than a deploy error. That is ADR-0004's stated trade, but it means a bad migration is discovered at runtime on Vercel rather than in CI, and CI only proves the migrations run on PGlite. The QA script's first step asks for the startup log line when readiness fails, precisely because wait-ready otherwise reports a bad migration as an environment failure.

The source-address rate limit is inert until a proxy sets x-forwarded-for, and there is no proxy in the compose environment QA drives — so the per-source half of TR-11 is not observable in QA at all. The honest cost of the other choice is a CGNAT-shaped one: when a proxy IS present and many users share one address, that shared bucket is refused once it trips. residual_risks names it and QA is told not to report it.

The health endpoint is unauthenticated by design, because a readiness poll cannot hold a session. It runs one indexed query and returns no data, so it is not an information leak — but it is a public route on a deployed app, and QA should confirm it leaks nothing beyond status, latency and which of the two fixed sentences it returned.

This ticket adds no money type, so the rule that makes TR-2 enforceable — a money value cannot be given a number without a type error — does not exist yet. It arrives with src/lib/money.ts in piece 4. Until then nothing in the codebase can be wrong about money, because nothing in it is money.

The route group (app) is what makes requireUser() run once for the signed-in shell. A later ticket that adds a screen outside the group without its own check would bypass it. The group is easy to forget precisely because it is invisible in a URL; a reviewer should check every new page lands inside it.

Sign-out is a bare control in the top bar rather than the profile menu docs/ui.md:204 specifies, because no menu primitive exists in the design system yet. The QA script suppresses a report of it, and this entry is here so a later ticket's council reads it as a known deviation to close rather than a decision that was already settled.
out_of_scope: Groups, members, invites, placeholder members, roles and every group's data — piece 2, per the ticket. The home screen's Create group action is a link into a screen that does not exist yet, and the ticket's own empty-state wording requires it to be there.

POST /api/dev/seed as a route handler, any fixture users, groups, expenses, payments or placeholder member, and the full idempotent seed — piece 9. scripts/seed.mjs exists in this ticket only so the verb is real and safe; it checks that the app is up and writes nothing, and piece 9 replaces its body with the call ADR-0007 specifies. See risks for the ADR-0007 guard collision piece 9 will inherit.

Any money value. No amount is parsed, split, formatted or rendered here, so src/lib/money.ts, the split types and src/lib/balances.ts are all piece 4's. The money UI primitive formats a bigint but nothing calls it yet.
Password reset and account deletion — the spec lists them as not in this version.

Session rotation on use and an absolute session cap beyond the 30-day cookie maxAge. The cookie expires and signing out revokes it, which is what TR-10 requires; shortening a stolen cookie's life is a defensible later change and naming it here means it is a decision rather than an oversight.

Redirecting an already-signed-in visitor away from /sign-in and /sign-up, and any policy on what happens to an existing session when someone signs up while signed in. The pages render for a signed-in visitor in this ticket because the QA script's double-submit step needs the form; a redirect is a product decision about the shell's edges, and the route group (app) already keeps the real surfaces behind the session check.

A root not-found page, a global-error boundary, and loading or error boundaries for the two auth screens. The auth screens reach an expected-failure state as a field error or a form message rendered inline, which is the state they can actually reach and is where the QA script looks for it; a 404 page and a global boundary are a screen's worth of design work that no criterion in this ticket asks for.

A persistent PGlite data directory and any PGLITE_DATA_DIR variable. This ticket's local database is in-process and in-memory, which is what makes the QA and CI story nothing-installed; persistence is a deploy concern, and it is also why the seeding script has no data directory to collide with.

The recorded decision for this issue (store the split rule with the expense, and rewrite TR-4 so an edit replaces that expense's stored payers and shares in one transaction). It binds pieces 3 and 4 and this ticket pre-empts none of it: there is no expense table, no split type and no amount in this data model. Naming it so the omission is deliberate rather than an oversight.

A Vercel project and a Neon database, neither of which exists. TR-27's README deploy guide — including the table that would document TABS_ENV — is piece 9's; this ticket adds only the environment-variable behaviour IAC-9 requires, documented in src/lib/env.ts and in its own error message.

Changing .sdlc/config.yml — in particular qa_auth.mode, which stays `none`, qa_auth.signup_url, which is /signup while the route is /sign-up, and verify.build, which stays empty. All are reserved paths and the maintainer's to change. QA drives the sign-up path from the running app's own link, exactly as the issue says it will, and is told the URL divergence is not a bug.
residual_risks: The per-source half of TR-11 is not observable anywhere in this pipeline. The compose environment has no proxy, so no request carries x-forwarded-for, and the plan exempts undetermined sources from the limit — the right trade, and it means the per-source rate limit has never executed in a real environment. QA and review should read the source-limit code rather than go looking for a browser symptom, and a later ticket that adds a proxy (or env.mode: preview, where Vercel does set the header) should be the one to prove it.

Nothing enforces the rule that only tests/helpers/pglite.ts may reach the database. The next ticket's integration test can import a page or a barrel that transitively constructs a real PGlite at import time and fail in a way that reads like a database bug rather than a rule violation. This order names the helper and states the rule; it cannot make an import illegal.

The vitest concurrency cap is a judgement, not a measurement. If scrypt at 128 MB per verification plus a WASM PGlite per file still exhausts a small runner with the cap in place, AC-1 goes red for an environment reason. It should be the first thing to loosen, and the suite is slow enough that raising it is a real trade.

Two browser behaviours are not covered by any criterion and are not code defects: a restored bfcache page after sign-out, and two tabs signing in as the same user where the second write replaces the first's cookie. Both are browser semantics rather than server-state problems, and neither is visible to the tests. QA may note them; they are not this ticket's failures.

The environment policy's one unverified framework assumption is whether a throw inside instrumentation register() halts the server. Both paths are specified — the health route's 503 and sdlc:ready's curl -f — so a wrong answer here degrades to 'QA reports blocked with a real reason' rather than to a silent misconfiguration. That is a mitigation, not a proof.
work_order.confidence_rationale: The diagnosis is verified rather than inferred, and the framework claims were re-derived from the code rather than inherited: I read guards.js and confirm both that a stubbed sdlc:seed fails ci-verify and — a correction neither the proposal nor I made before the critique raised it — that the liveness BODY is not what satisfies the guard, the command string is; I also confirmed reservedChanges allows filling a stub exactly once, so the package.json edit raises no reserved hit; and both the proposal and the critique independently read the next@16.3.0 tarball and agree that `next start` is production and that `next build` never calls register(). The design is greenfield against a written architecture with no existing code to break, and the split's own acceptance list maps one-to-one onto AC-1..AC-11. What holds the number at 77 rather than higher is four things I cannot check from here, each given a one-line fallback or a mitigation rather than a second council: whether pg_advisory_lock and hashtext exist on PGlite 0.5.8, whether drizzle-kit's generated SQL runs unchanged on PGlite, whether a throw inside register() halts the server (mitigated by the health route's second gate, so it degrades to a blocked report rather than a silent misconfiguration), and whether the QA browser will store a Secure cookie over http://localhost. It is below the proposal's 82 because the review was right three times in ways that would each have failed the run — an unexecutable QA script, a strict-mode policy that made the test process itself throw, and a migrator that read a table no file created — which says the plan's self-assessment was a little generous. What would move it up: one CI run of this branch, since AC-1, AC-3 and AC-11 between them exercise all four unknowns in about four minutes. What would move it down: if the health route's accessor seam turns out not to make GET callable under vitest, AC-2 would move to a browser harness — a change of proof, not of requirement, but it is the one place a criterion I rewrote could still need reshaping.
work_order.debate_summary:
The critique was right about the diagnosis and right about a great deal, including three things that would each have failed this run, and I rejected two of its prescriptions on the evidence rather than on taste.

**Accepted, and ranked above the critique itself ranked them.**

(1) The qa_script was unexecutable in order — the sharpest finding, because it is the only one that fails no matter how good the code is. v2 asked QA to sign out and to use a registered email two steps before the only sign-up in the script, and qa_auth.mode is `none`, so no fixture account exists. Steps 5 and 6 are AC-7's only browser verification. I did more than reorder: the byte-identity comparison and the sixth-then-seventh boundary now use two different accounts (qa2 and qa1), because the account limit is per key and running the wrong-password comparison against the same account would leave a failure row that makes the seventh attempt's arithmetic wrong. Sign-ups come first; the boundary step is unchanged in wording and now has a real account under it.

(2) The migrations table. This arrived as the ninth of ten `missed_edge_cases` and it is the most severe defect in the plan. v2's migrate() read the applied set 'from the migrations table' while schema.ts created only users, sessions and login_attempts — so on the first boot, on an empty database, the read throws before a single table exists. v2 also committed no migration SQL at all, which is the same failure one step later: an empty list means an empty database. Either kills the boot, and with it AC-1's second half, AC-3, AC-4 and every browser criterion. The migrator now creates its own bookkeeping table as its first statement, and the generated first migration is committed rather than merely generated.

(3) The strict-by-default environment policy reached everything. The critique filed the `npm run dev` half as a major finding against TR-22, and it is right: Next skips register() only under phase-production-build, so `next dev` runs it and a bare `next dev` throws. But the same gap is wider than the critique said, and this is the part neither the proposal nor the critique fully stated — sdlc:verify invokes `vitest run` DIRECTLY, so a prefix on the `test` script would not reach the suite, and every test that touches config() (auth.ts for the HMAC key, the actions, the health route) throws with TABS_ENV unset. The suite was red before it started. The fix is therefore two places, not one: the prefix on every script that reaches config(), and `test.env.TABS_ENV = 'local'` in vitest.config.ts, which is the declaration that actually reaches `vitest run`.

(4) AC-2's 503 half was unreachable, for the same reason, and the fix is the critique's option (a): the health route catches a config failure and answers 503 rather than throwing. I modified it in one respect — a configuration fault must not be reported with the database's fixed sentence, so the route carries two fixed sentences and neither is the driver's text. The tripwire is unaffected, since curl -f treats 503 as failure.

(5) The missing cookie seam. tests/helpers/request.ts specified a `cookies()` shim the actions 'read through', with no such seam in auth.ts — and the natural implementation imports next/headers directly, so the shim would have been dead code and AC-5, AC-6, AC-7 and AC-11 would have depended on a module patch nobody described. src/lib/cookies.ts is now a file in its own right, named as the single module that imports next/headers, with the cookie name as a constant both writers share.

(6) `login_attempts.succeeded` was a column nothing wrote. Accepted as a real gap, with the diagnosis as given — but the remedy is mine, not the critique's; see the disagreement below.

(7) No Client Component anywhere in files[], while docs/ui.md:210 requires a disabled 'Signing in…' button, the QA script asserts 'Creating account…', and pending state from a Server Action requires useActionState. The plan had an assertion no file could satisfy. auth-form.tsx and settings-form.tsx now carry it, (app)/error.tsx and ui/dialog.tsx are marked 'use client' deliberately, and Button stays presentational so conventions.md's rule survives.

(8) The source limit's boundary, which the critique caught by turning v2's own argument against it: v2 fixed the account off-by-one in five places and left the sibling constant in exactly the ambiguous phrasing, so 'twenty attempts are refused' did not say whether the twentieth or the twenty-first is. It now reads 'once twenty failures from that source already exist, so the twenty-first attempt is refused without verifying the password at all', repeated verbatim in AC-7, auth.ts and the integration test.

(9) The named-but-absent tsconfig.eslint.json fallback (dropped in favour of committing to projectService: true), the /signup vs /sign-up divergence in the QA script's do-not-report list, the undocumented local defaults including the HMAC key, the vitest pool sizing against 128 MB scrypt buffers, the 'exactly one h1' assertion that could only prove 'at most one' until the test composes a real screen, and the profile-menu deviation moved from the QA script's suppressions into risks[] where a later council will read it.

**Rejected — the source bucket should count successes.** The critique's fix for `succeeded` was that the source predicate counts all attempts and successes, with a new test asserting a successful sign-in still counts against the source bucket. That would refuse a correct password for having signed in twenty times in fifteen minutes. TR-11's subject is failed sign-ins — 'Failed sign-ins are rate-limited per account and per source address' — and a lockout the requirement does not ask for is the same class of harm the account-limit design exists to avoid. So both predicates count `succeeded = false`, every attempt still writes a row with its true value (the column earns its keep and there is an audit trail), and a success clears that account's failure rows. The critique was right that the column was dead and right that the counting question had to be answered; the answer it gave is the one I declined.

**Corrected — the council's own reasoning about the seed, in the critique's favour.** Both the proposal and v1's arbiter argued at length that scripts/seed.mjs needs a non-trivial BODY to satisfy verify-is-real. Reading guards.js, isTrivialScript splits on &&/||/; and demands every segment be exit/true/:/echo, so `node scripts/seed.mjs` already passes on the command string alone. The critique caught this. The conclusion is unchanged and the body stays — it is safe, it honours ADR-0007's dependency on the app being up, and it cannot corrupt anything — but the plan's stated mechanism was wrong, and I have said so rather than letting a correct outcome rest on a false claim an implementer might rely on later.

**Dismissed as noise or as a matter the plan already covers.** The browser back-stack and two-tab cases are browser semantics rather than code defects and are in residual_risks. Email length/shape bounds, the WINDOW comparison operator, and rejecting rather than truncating a non-three-letter currency are one-line decisions folded into files[] rather than findings of their own. The 'nothing may import the client singleton from a test' rule is enforced by nothing, which is true and is in residual_risks as the honest version of that sentence. environmentMatchGlobs is resolved by specifying per-file docblocks, which is the stable path, rather than as a finding. The finding that plan/ artifacts trip hasProductCode() is a correct reading of the code and a non-conclusion: this branch lands src/ regardless, and a docs-only branch still stands down.

**Where I extended both.** Beyond the critique: the committed migration SQL (the plan named the generator, never its output), the seeded QA accounts being two rather than one, the window operator being stated as strictly greater so the boundary is testable at all, and the health route's two-sentence answer.

**The call I am least sure of.** Exempting undetermined source addresses from the rate limit. It is defensible and it is the only one that makes QA runnable at all, but it means the per-source half of TR-11 is inert in every environment this pipeline can observe, and I have put that in residual_risks, in risks and in the QA script's do-not-report list rather than leaving it to be discovered by a reader who assumes the opposite.
